summary: Russia has launched massive Geran-5 missile-drone strikes on Kyiv and central Ukraine while relocating armed strategic bombers to Olenya airfield, signaling a potential large-scale missile attack. The Russian army liberated the villages of Shirokoye and Shevchenkovo in the Kharkov region. Trump stated Ukraine agreed not to strike Russian energy facilities, while Ukraine's daily war cost reached $190 million.
key_points: Russia has stockpiled a large number of drones capable of striking Ukraine from various directions throughout the day, according to Air Force spokesman Ignat during the national telethon. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/33242)

Three Tu-95MS strategic bombers were relocated from the Far East to Olenya airfield, armed with cruise missiles, alongside two already stationed there and three armed Tu-160s, posing a threat of a massive missile strike. (Source: @eRadarrua/113272)
The Russian army liberated the villages of Shirokoye and Shevchenkovo in the Kharkov region, according to a statement from ukr_leaks_eng. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/33245)
Trump stated that Ukraine agreed not to strike Russian energy facilities, according to a TASS report. (Source: @tass_agency/395362)

Geran-5 drones fly at up to 600 km/h with a 90 kg warhead out to 1,000 km, and Ukrainian air defense intercepts only about 60 percent of them, according to Financial Times analysis cited by ukr_leaks_eng. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/33235)

Ukraine's daily cost of war in 2026 reached $190 million, $50 million more than 2024, due to army expansion and increased family support payments, according to budget committee head Ryksolana Pidlasa. (Source: @UkraineNow/84095)
Swiss authorities are ready to accept a new round of trilateral negotiations on Ukraine, according to a TASS report citing the Swiss MFA spokesperson. (Source: @tass_agency/395371)

sections.threat_assessment: Russia is conducting sustained mass drone and missile strikes against Ukrainian civilian and energy infrastructure from multiple directions, with Geran-5 drones presenting a growing interception challenge due to their 600 km/h speed and 1,000 km range. The relocation of armed Tu-95MS and Tu-160 strategic bombers to Olenya airfield signals a credible threat of a large-scale cruise missile strike in the near term. Russia's stockpiling of drones and liberation of villages in Kharkiv region indicate both offensive and defensive momentum. The stated Ukrainian agreement not to strike Russian energy facilities, if confirmed, would represent a significant constraint on Ukraine's operational flexibility.
sections.regional_response: Polish Foreign Minister Sikorski has called on NATO to step up military exercises near the Kaliningrad borders to force Russia to redeploy troops from Ukraine, while also asserting that NATO would easily defeat Russia in a conflict due to Europe's overwhelming air superiority. Switzerland has signaled readiness to accept a new round of trilateral negotiations on Ukraine. Russia's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova has publicly criticized Sikorski's statements about Poland's ability to quickly defeat Russia, reflecting escalating diplomatic tensions between NATO and Russia.
sections.intelligence_notes: The Geran-5 represents a generational shift in Russian unmanned warfare, with a 90 kg warhead, 600 km/h speed, and AI-assisted terminal guidance, fielded at a fraction of the cost of Kalibr or Kh-101 cruise missiles. Ukraine's 67 companies are reportedly working on countermeasures, but the industrial asymmetry remains stark as air-defense missiles cannot be improvised like interceptor drones. Internal Ukrainian political instability is evident with the removal of Prosecutor General Kravchenko and the investigation into NABU Director Krivonos, potentially affecting governance continuity during active hostilities.
